shared_elements: monolithic upright pillar/statue treated as a body
low-relief arm/hand rendered on the shaft
low-relief motifs applied to a plain vertical stone body
banded or belt-like horizontal relief across the shaft
justification: Both depict an upright monolithic form conceived as a body, with shallow relief limbs — notably a schematic hand/arm laid flat against the lower part of the shaft — plus additional relief motifs (a disc/rounded boss and a horizontal belt-like band in A) applied to an otherwise plain vertical surface. The clearest difference is that B carries a prominent quadruped animal in high relief descending head-down on the shaft, with no comparable creature in A, while A's upper zone is dominated by a broad carved head/headdress with dense incised ornament absent in B.
